description:
Site Administrator (Construction) Full-time

We are currently recruiting on behalf of a well-established construction contractor for an experienced Site Administrator to join their project team.

This is an excellent opportunity for an organised and proactive administrator who has previous experience working within the construction industry and enjoys supporting busy site teams.

The Role

- Coordinating site meetings and taking minutes where required.

title: HR / Office Manager
description:
HR AND OFFICE MANAGER
MANCHESTER, OFFICE BASED
42,000- 45,000 DOE + BENEFITS

Are you an Office Manager with facilities management industry experience looking for a varied role with responsibility across office operations and HR?

Get Recruited is partnering with an established facilities management business to recruit an HR and Office Manager for its Manchester head office.

Supporting a business who has employees across the North West, this HR and Office Manager position has a strong emphasis on office management, administration and coordination, alongside practical HR responsibilities.
You'll keep head office running smoothly, support managers and improve processes for a workforce comprising both full-time and part-time employees.

This opportunity would suit an Office Manager, HR and Office Manager, Office and Administration Manager or Business Support Manager with experience working within the facilities management industry.

THE HR AND OFFICE MANAGER ROLE:
As HR and Office Manager, you'll take ownership of day-to-day office operations while ensuring people administration is organised, accurate and consistent.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Overseeing the smooth running of head office administration and coordinating daily priorities.
- Establishing clear responsibilities and efficient ways of working across office operations.
- Acting as a central point of contact for managers and employees across the business.
- Improving administrative systems, workflows and communication to reduce duplication and manual tasks.

- Coordinating recruitment, interviews, offers, pre-employment checks and onboarding.
- Supporting managers with employee relations, absence management, probation reviews and performance processes.
- Ensuring company policies and procedures are applied consistently.
- Coordinating training and mandatory compliance requirements.
- Providing clear updates and people information to senior leadership.

The HR and Office Manager will bring organisation, consistency and accountability to a busy head office, helping managers access the information and support they need.

THE PERSON:
We're looking for an experienced Office Manager or HR and Office Manager who understands the demands of supporting an operational workforce across multiple locations.
You will have:
- Experience within the facilities management or similar industry is essential.
- Strong office management and administration experience within facilities management.
- Practical HR experience, including employee records, recruitment, onboarding and supporting people matters.
- Organised with the ability to manage competing priorities.
- Confident communication skills when working with employees, operational managers and senior leadership.
- A proactive approach to improving processes and resolving problems.
- The confidence to maintain standards and handle challenging conversations professionally.
- Strong attention to detail and discretion when handling confidential information.
- The ability to take ownership and follow actions through to completion.

Experience as an Office and Administration Manager, Business Support Manager, People Operations Manager or HR and Office Manager would be relevant, provided you have the required facilities management background.
A CIPD qualification, or progress towards one, would be advantageous.

This HR and Office Manager role is fully office based at the Manchester head office.

- Free on-site parking.
- Company pension scheme.
- Holiday entitlement increasing with service.

- Team events and socials, including theatre trips and go-karting.
- Direct exposure to senior leadership.

title: HR Manager
description:
Are you a HR leader looking to influence a forward thinking, values-led organisation which helps give children the best possible start in life?

The first internal role of its kind at Home-Start HOST, their new HR Manager will help them ensure families with young children flourish during the years of early childhood. You'll support them to do this through expertly managing the HR function, shaping organisational culture and delivering training to upskill leaders.

Salary: £42,839-£46,142 pro rata (FTE, 36 hours per week), depending on experience.
Contract: Permanent, part-time, 24 hours per week. Reduced hours and flexible working considered.
Location: Hybrid, mostly at home, but also present at Audenshaw office.
Benefits: 24 days of annual leave plus bank holidays, increasing to 29 days after 5 years of service (pro rata), up to 6% employer pension contribution, flexible working arrangements and cycle to work scheme.

You'll need to be onsite for team meetings twice a month, plus some additional days to support training and development of the team.

About the charity

Home-Start HOST works alongside families with young children, empowering them to build confidence, strengthen relationships and create positive, resilient futures. They do this through a wide range of services, including one-to-one support in the home, early learning, breastfeeding, perinatal support and their baby bank, which supports 100 families a month.

They know how tough parenting can be and the difference the right support can make.

Part of the Home-Start UK network, they support parents across Tameside, Oldham, Stockport, Bolton & Glossop.

About the role

This is an especially exciting role, as Home-Start HOST's first-ever in-house HR lead. Your remit will include staff recruitment, development, training, welfare and equality, and diversity and inclusion.

You will take responsibility for the functionality of HR processes and policies across the organisation, keeping on top of changes or updates to UK employment law, HR best practice, pay & benefits and you'll work closely with the CEO and board to ensure the organisation remains compliant.

You'll oversee recruitment processes for staff and volunteers, ensuring fairness and inclusion are always front and centre and support line managers to feel confident and capable when it comes to HR and employee relations.

This is a unique and special opportunity to grow a HR function from the ground up, driving policy and influencing the culture of Home-Start HOST.

About you

This role would suit an experienced, knowledgeable and conscientious HR professional who's passionate about helping an organisation stay true to its values, put people at the heart of its decisions and maintain robust, effective HR practices.

Key attributes we're looking for in our new HR Manager include:
- CIPD Level 5 or above
- Knowledge and experience of applying UK employment law and HR best practice
- Experience across the breadth of HR; employee relations, recruitment and policy development
- Passion and experience of fostering a values-led, inclusive culture
- Experience delivering training

Most importantly, you believe in supporting parents when they need it most and helping set children up for positive and healthy futures.

How to apply

If you're keen to get stuck into an HR leadership role where you'll have the autonomy of a smaller organisation, alongside the support of a national network, we'd love to hear from you.

Please send a copy of your profile or CV to Amelia Lee at Charity People as the first step.

Deadline: 9am on Friday 6th November

Charity People is a forward thinking, inclusive organisation that actively and deliberately promotes equity, diversity and inclusion. We know organisations thrive when inclusion is at the forefront. We evidence our commitment by matching charity needs with the skills and experience of candidates irrespective of background e.g. age, disability (including hidden disabilities), gender, gender identity or gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, or sexual orientation. We do this because we believe that greater diversity leads to greater results for the charities we work with.

Third-party job sites
We've noticed that there's been an increase in our job ads being published on sites that we have no affiliation with.
Please make sure you only apply via one of our legitimate and verified vacancies. A list of affiliated sites can be found on the Charity People website where you'll also find some useful dos and don'ts when applying for jobs. If you have any concerns or would like to verify a vacancy, please contact Charity People directly.

Closing date: 04/11/2026, 23:55

Position Type: Full Time

The Independent Football Regulator (IFR) has been established to protect and promote the sustainability of English football, for the benefit of fans and the local communities football clubs serve.

The IFR will help improve financial sustainability of clubs, ensure resilience across the leagues, and safeguard the heritage of English football. It will operate a licensing regime; set corporate governance standards and monitor, protect, and promote financial resilience. It will also enforce compliance with requirements on financial regulation, club ownership and directors, fan engagement, and heritage protection.

The IFR will also have powers to prohibit clubs from joining competitions that are not fair or meritocratic, or that threaten the heritage or sustainability of English football.

Key Responsibilities
- Provide support to the Director, Deputy Director and Head of the Supervision Office, developing a strong understanding of the Football Regulator's priorities, operating environment and the wider football industry.
- Manage the time and priorities of the Director, Deputy Director and Head of the Supervision Office, ensuring diaries, meetings and travel align with business needs and strategic objectives.

- Undertake the supervision of clubs when required, acting as a key point of contact and supporting engagement with external stakeholders.
- Support the oversight of high-risk clubs, identifying emerging risks, trends and issues requiring regulatory attention.
- Maintain effective collaboration between the IFR and key football competition authorities, including the Premier League, EFL and National League.
- Work closely with colleagues at all levels, representing the Director's Office and helping to drive departmental priorities.
- Build strong working relationships with senior leaders across the Supervision Directorate and the wider organisation.
- Manage complex and sensitive issues relating to regulated clubs and corporate matters, while delivering high-quality reporting, briefings and governance support.

Essential Requirements
- The ability to work at pace, driving progress in the face of a range of competing views and being calm and resilient in pressurised situations.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to balance competing priorities and pressure.
- Strategic thinking to understand the sensitivities of the brief and spot the key issues and risks before they arise.
- Leadership skills and ability to form effective working relationships with colleagues and stakeholders internally and externally, and at various levels of seniority.
- Strategic analysis skills to provide challenge and fresh ideas across a broad range of issues and in response to breaking events.

- Knowledge of the football industry.

title: Document Controller
description:
Document Controller

Facade Remediation Contractor

Location: Manchester City Centre - Office-based, with occasional travel to project sites
Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience
Contract: Full-time, permanent

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced and highly organised Document Controller to join a growing facade remediation contractor.

The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting the delivery of our facade remediation projects, ensuring that all project documentation is accurately controlled, maintained and distributed. Working closely with project managers, site teams, commercial teams, consultants and subcontractors, you will be responsible for maintaining robust document control procedures and ensuring that project information is managed efficiently throughout the project lifecycle.

Previous experience using Viewpoint 4 Projects is essential for this role. We are looking for someone who can confidently manage construction documentation within the platform and understands the importance of accurate revision control, document tracking and maintaining comprehensive project records.

This is an office-based position, with occasional travel to project sites as required.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage and maintain project documentation through Viewpoint 4 Projects, ensuring all information is correctly uploaded, recorded, distributed and controlled.
- Maintain document registers, drawing registers, revision histories and transmittal records across multiple projects.
- Ensure the correct and latest revisions of drawings, specifications and technical documents are available to relevant project stakeholders.
- Upload, issue and track drawings, technical submissions, specifications, reports, risk assessments and method statements.
- Monitor document review and approval workflows, following up with project teams, consultants and subcontractors on outstanding submissions.
- Maintain accurate records of quality assurance documentation, inspection and test records, photographic evidence and project compliance information.
- Assist with the preparation and collation of project handover packs, operation and maintenance manuals, health and safety files and completion documentation.
- Support the management of facade remediation documentation, including material approvals, product data, fire safety information and other relevant compliance records.

You will play an important part in ensuring materials and services are available when needed, deliveries arrive on time and stock levels are maintained to support business operations.

The Role

- Coordinating the purchasing of raw materials, consumables and services to meet operational and production requirements.

- Building and maintaining effective relationships with suppliers, monitoring service levels and helping to resolve delivery, quality and pricing issues.
- Monitoring stock levels and material availability to support production schedules and minimise shortages or excess inventory.
- Liaising with suppliers, logistics partners, warehouse and production teams to coordinate deliveries and resolve stock discrepancies.

We are looking for an organised and commercially minded individual with previous experience in purchasing, procurement or supply chain coordination, ideally within a manufacturing, engineering or similar operational environment.

You will be comfortable managing multiple priorities, communicating with suppliers and internal departments, and taking a proactive approach to resolving issues.

You should also have:
- Experience in purchasing, supplier coordination or supply chain operations.
- A good understanding of procurement processes, stock control and delivery coordination.

description: Salford Primary Care Together (SPCT) Community Interest Company (CIC) is looking for experienced Medical Administrators to join our dedicated practice team within Salford Little Hulton - 1 x 37.5 hour vacancy You could be required to work across our other SPCT sites which are: Eccles and Willow Tree, subject to organisational requirement. JOB PURPOSE As a Medical Administrator it will be your responsibility to aid in the seamless running of the practice by the completion of administrative tasks in an efficient and accurate manner. You will have strong and consistent communication skills which will be utilised in a friendly approach towards all patients, visitors and colleagues. You will be able to work well collaboratively as well as individually in a fast-paced, care centric environment to produce the highest quality of patient care, and organisational priority here at Salford Primary Care Together. Offer general assistance to the Practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone. Undertake a variety of administrative duties to assist in the smooth running of the Practice including the provision of secretarial and clerical support to clinical staff and other members of the Practice team. Facilitate effective communication between patients, members the primary healthcare team, secondary care and other associated healthcare agencies. Scanning referral letters on to patients records if required. Liaising with the hospitals and secondary care about patient appointment and test result queries. Recording of incoming and outgoing insurance reports, allocating said reports to the Doctors and monitoring that payment is received. Photocopying of medical records when requested by Insurance Companies, Solicitors or Doctors. Managing the stock levels and ordering of all secretarial and practice stationery. As an Administrator it will be your responsibility to work with the team to help with the seamless running of the practice by the completion of administrative tasks in an efficient and accurate manner. You will have strong and consistent communication skills which will be utilised in a friendly approach towards all patients, visitors and colleagues. You will be able to work well collaboratively as well as individually in a fast-paced, care centric environment to produce high quality patient care. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES OF THE ROLE To receive patients at the surgery in a friendly manner, efficiently checking-in those with booked appointments. To receive and make telephone calls, using a helpful and problem-solving approach. To maintain good housekeeping of the admin and reception areas as well as maintain the security of the building by ensuring visitors are signed in/out. Report any issues that will affect the smooth running of the practice to your line manager. To monitor flow of patients and inform patients and staff of any delays or possible problems. To ensure that patients with an urgent medical need are brought to the attention of the clinical staff and are dealt with in a logical and non-disruptive manner. To explain practice arrangements and formal requirements to existing and new patients and those seeking temporary registration and ensure that the necessary registration procedures are completed in a timely manner. Undertake a variety of administrative duties to assist in the smooth running of the Practice including the provision of administrative and clerical support to clinical staff and other members of the Practice team. To gain comperency, as directed, in the use of IT applications in support of your role; including, but restricted to: EMIS, DocMan, X-On (Surgery Connect), AccuRx and Bright HR. To book appointments and recalls, ensuring sufficient information is recorded to enable clinical staff to access the patients record and to prioritise their workload. To process prescription requests as directed. To gain compertency in clinical coding. Typing and/or processing referral letters and general correspondence. Processing referrrals and dealing with queries on the NHS e-referral system. Keeping referral templates and forms within the clinical system up to date. Scanning correspondence on to patients records as required. Liaising with the hospitals and secondary care about patient appointments and test result queries. Dealing with queries raised by Clinicians, The Management team and Patients. Processing requests from patients and others regarding medical records and medical information including ensuring appropriate consent is in place and payment is received in line with SPCT procedures.

title: Medical Receptionist
location: Manchester, M26 2TQ, BURY, BL9 0NJ, BURY, BL8 4DR, BURY, BL8 4AD
description: We are a GP Practice with a multi skilled clinical team that works across four sites across Bury (in Bury town centre, Greenmount, Tottington and Radcliffe). We are looking for a new Medical Receptionists to join our experienced and friendly reception team. No two days will be the same in this rewarding, patient facing role where the postholder will have the opportunity to get involved in a wide range of duties at our busy general practice. You will support patients getting in touch by phone and in person at reception, using your care navigation skills to reach the best outcome to meet their needs. Variety is important in any role, and there will be opportunities to get involved in a range of administrative tasks across the working week. Full training will be provided to ensure you can thrive in the role. Investing in our team is important to us, and in return for your commitment we can offer a competitive rate of pay, recognised continuous NHS service, NHS Pension scheme enrolment and continued professional development. Shifts will fall Monday to Friday between 8:00am and 6:30pm. Flexibility is required, as shifts may cover any part of these hours. Check out the detailed job summary on this page and get in touch. The receptionist/admin role at Tower Family Healthcare requires enthusiastic, friendly, positive, professional individuals who enjoy working as part of a team and strive to deliver a high standard of service to patients and public in an efficient, effective, courteous and confidential manner. The role is also to provide support to the clinicians (both doctors and nurses) and the leadership team to meet the requirements of the practice We are looking for a friendly, professional, and highly organised individual to join our team as a Medical Receptionist. This is a key frontline role, responsible for providing a welcoming and efficient service to our patients both face-to-face and over the telephone. You will support the smooth running of the practice by managing appointments, handling patient enquiries, maintaining accurate records, and assisting clinical and administrative teams. The role involves a wide variety of duties including appointment scheduling, message handling, prescription processing, maintaining clinical rooms, managing referrals, and liaising with a range of healthcare professionals and external agencies. You will also carry out general administrative tasks such as filing, photocopying, scanning, typing, and updating patient information systems. Attention to detail, excellent communication skills, and the ability to follow practice policies and procedures are essential. You will be required to use clinical systems such as EMIS, as well as support the team with daily checklists and ad-hoc duties to ensure the practice operates safely and effectively. This is a busy and rewarding role working at the heart of patient care, where your contribution will help support both patients and the wider clinical team.

title: Experienced Medical Receptionist
description: We are a friendly and supportive GP practice located in Central Manchester seeking a full time experienced receptionist/administrative. It is an exciting opportunity for an enthusiastic individual to join our dynamic team. The main duties of the position include answering the telephone, working at the reception front desk, managing and booking appointments, EMIS tasks, Docman scanning and attaching, handling emails, taking prescription requests, registering patients, processing referrals and performing some general administrative duties. You will receive full support. To undertake a variety of reception and administration duties to assist in the smooth running of the Practice and provide a high level of service to patients, doctors, nurses and other members of the Practice team. Main Duties Make new and follow-up patient appointments in a timely manner using the IT system (EMIS web) Receive and direct patients to the correct professional or service Act as chaperone Contact the interpretation service for patients as required Maintain accurate records of patient care in electronic format using the correct codes Prepare reception area for incoming colleagues, participate hand over between shifts Take telephone messages and general enquiries, direct as necessary to GP Process incoming and outgoing correspondence, including managing workflow tasks Manage all queries (including administrative queries) as necessary in an efficient manner Input data into the patient's healthcare records as necessary Support the team in the effective use of searches, audits and recalls Be aware of confidentiality and offer patients the opportunity to go to a confidentiality booth if they are distressed or imparting sensitive information General Observe health and safety guidelines at all times Participate in any training programme implemented by the Practice Any other reasonable duties as necessary

title: Senior Receptionist
description: We are seeking an experienced and highly motivated Senior Receptionist to join our busy GP practice. This is an excellent opportunity for an organised and patient-focused individual to play a key role in supporting the smooth running of our reception team and delivering exceptional customer service to our patients. Acting as a senior member of the reception team and providing day-to-day support to reception staff. Managing and resolving patient queries, concerns, and complaints in a professional and empathetic manner. Providing excellent customer service both face-to-face and over the telephone. Scheduling appointments and assisting patients with access to practice services. Supporting the management of staff rotas, including adding schedules and maintaining rotas within EMIS Web. Assisting with practice administration and ensuring reception processes are followed efficiently. Working collaboratively with clinical and administrative teams to support patient care. Maintaining patient confidentiality at all times in line with NHS and GDPR requirements The Senior Receptionist plays a key role in supporting the day-to-day management of the reception function, ensuring that patients receive a professional, efficient, and welcoming service at all times. As a senior member of the administrative team, you will provide guidance and support to reception staff, assist with the smooth running of practice operations, and help maintain high standards of patient care. The role involves managing patient enquiries and resolving issues effectively, coordinating appointments, maintaining staff rotas and schedules within EMIS Web, and supporting the delivery of administrative processes across the practice. You will work closely with clinicians, management, and administrative colleagues to ensure services are delivered efficiently and in line with practice policies, NHS requirements, and patient needs. The successful candidate will possess excellent communication, organisational, and problem-solving skills, with experience in a GP practice environment and a commitment to providing outstanding patient service. Knowledge of EMIS Web and an understanding of QOF processes are highly desirable. All duties must be carried out with strict adherence to patient confidentiality, GDPR requirements, and NHS standards.
